description: GrantFinder starter grant database: national, Catholic and Texas grant programs that a Catholic school or parish can apply to, each checked against the funder's own site on its last_verified date (deadlines, amounts, eligibility, whether religious organizations may apply). Refreshed monthly by the grant-research skill. Deadlines and amounts change: always confirm on the funder's website before applying.

grants.grant_name: Advancing Our Mission Grants for Teachers and Staff
grants.funder: Catholic Schools Office, Diocese of Austin (Advancing Our Mission Endowment, Catholic Foundation - Diocese of Austin)
grants.deadline_notes: Awarded each year by the Catholic Schools Office; the application window and form are posted on the diocesan schools site (csdatx.org/aomgrants), which blocks automated checks, so the current deadline is unconfirmed.
grants.amount: Varies (about $40,000 awarded in total each year)
grants.typical_award: About $40,000 awarded per year in total (diocesan magazine)
grants.description: Annual grants from a $1 million endowment created by the Encountering Christ campaign, letting teachers and staff of Diocese of Austin Catholic schools fund projects that impact student learning in and out of the classroom.
grants.geography: Catholic schools of the Diocese of Austin only
grants.eligibility_notes: Per the program page title, teachers and staff at diocesan Catholic schools apply for classroom or school projects. Individual award limits and the current cycle dates could not be confirmed from the official page.

grants.funder: Catholic Schools Office, Diocese of Austin (Catholic School Endowment, Catholic Foundation - Diocese of Austin)
grants.deadline_notes: Families apply each year through the diocesan Catholic Schools Office for the following school year; the application page (csdatx.org/beaconofhope) blocks automated checks, so the 2027-2028 dates are unconfirmed.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.typical_award: 2023-24: $200,000 to 283 students (about $700 per student; diocesan magazine)
grants.description: Diocesan tuition scholarships for students at Diocese of Austin Catholic schools, now backed by a $5 million Catholic School Endowment created by the Encountering Christ campaign to provide tuition assistance to families seeking a Catholic education.
grants.geography: Catholic schools of the Diocese of Austin only
grants.eligibility_notes: Families of students at diocesan Catholic schools apply (not the school itself). Current criteria and deadlines could not be confirmed from the official page.
focus_areas: Tuition assistance for families seeking a Catholic education

grants.funder: Burkitt Foundation (administered by El Paso Community Foundation)
grants.deadline_notes: Application opens July 1 and is due August 1 through the El Paso Community Foundation grant portal (applications stay open about 30 days). One request per funding source in any 12-month period; prior grant reports must be filed first.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: Perpetual fund that supports Catholic K-12 schools in three Texas dioceses (plus hunger and nutrition services in El Paso County). Schools complete supplemental Catholic questions, including their Official Catholic Directory listing.
grants.geography: Catholic K-12 schools in the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston, Archdiocese of San Antonio and Diocese of El Paso only (not Diocese of Austin)
grants.eligibility_notes: Catholic K-12 schools in the three named dioceses; supplemental 'Catholic Directory Listing' questions required. EPCF's general policy limits grants to religious organizations for religious purposes, but this fund exists specifically for Catholic schools.
focus_areas: Catholic schools (K-12) in Galveston-Houston, San Antonio and El Paso
Hunger and nutrition services in El Paso County

grants.grant_name: Tuition Grant Program for Catholic Elementary Schools
grants.funder: The George and Mary Kremer Foundation
grants.deadline_notes: Schools not yet participating email a School Profile Application by January 31, 2027 for the 2027-2028 school year (on or after February 1 counts toward 2028-2029). The advisory board meets in early March; participating schools are invited by early April and submit school profiles and student applications by early May; checks are mailed in early September.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: National tuition assistance grants paid to Catholic elementary schools on behalf of children from financially challenged families; principals select the students based mainly on financial need. In 2026-2027 grants reached about 3,400 students in 371 schools.
grants.geography: National (continental United States)
grants.eligibility_notes: Catholic elementary school (grades K-8 or any of them) listed in the current Official Catholic Directory, located in the continental U.S., and not tuition-free. The school applies, not families. Applications by email only.
focus_areas: Tuition assistance for children from financially challenged families

grants.deadline_notes: Annual window; the 2026 round accepted applications via SurveyMonkey Apply February 13 - May 11, 2026. The 2027 window has not been posted. 501(c)(3) organizations complete their own application after nomination by the local Area; local projects without a 501(c)(3) are submitted by the Area Chair.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: Annual grants to tax-exempt organizations and local projects that serve the sick and the poor and in which Order of Malta members actively volunteer. Each Area's grant committee recommends awards from its allocation.
grants.geography: Organizations where American Association members volunteer; Texas Areas listed: Dallas and Houston
grants.eligibility_notes: Members of the Order must be actively involved in the applying organization or project, so a parish ministry needs a local Knight or Dame as its champion. Area budget ranges are shared by members.
focus_areas: Service to the sick and the poor
Defense and witness of the Catholic faith
Local Area projects such as backpack programs and Malta Walks

grants.grant_name: Black and Indian Mission Office Diocesan Grants
grants.deadline_notes: Applied for by the diocese, not the parish or school. Applications for the 2027 grant year are closed; the next window is not yet posted. A parish or school would ask its diocesan office to include its program.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: Grants to dioceses with African American or Native American/Alaska Native communities for evangelization and ministry, including tuition assistance for African American and Native American students in Catholic schools, parish and school religious education, faith formation and rural parish subsidies.
grants.geography: National (through the diocese)
grants.eligibility_notes: Diocese is the applicant; open to all dioceses with African American and Native American/Alaska Native communities. Parishes and schools benefit through the diocesan request.
focus_areas: African American and Native American evangelization and ministry programs
Tuition assistance for African American and Native American Catholic school students
Religious education in parishes and Catholic schools

grants.grant_name: Catholic Campaign for Human Development Local Grants (Diocese of Austin)
grants.funder: Diocese of Austin, Secretariat for Life, Charity and Justice (local 25% share of the CCHD collection)
grants.deadline_notes: Funded from the 25% of the November CCHD collection that stays in the diocese; no public application window was found. Contact the diocesan Secretariat for Life, Charity and Justice through the diocesan website.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: Local anti-poverty grants to organizations and groups in the Diocese of Austin that help people stay out of poverty. Recent local recipients included permanent-housing and Habitat for Humanity programs, a maternity home, a shelter and pregnancy-and-parenting rental-assistance programs.
grants.geography: Diocese of Austin only
grants.eligibility_notes: Local criteria are not published online, and national CCHD rules (low-income leadership, no direct service as main focus) may also apply, so whether a parish or school can apply as itself is unconfirmed. Confirm with the diocese.
focus_areas: Helping people stay out of poverty
Support for pregnant women and families in crisis

grants.deadline_notes: Funding requests are due May 1 for dioceses on a January-December financial year and November 1 for dioceses on a July-June fiscal year; the diocese submits through Catholic Extension's online grant portal and funds are disbursed quarterly.
grants.amount: Varies (no published range)
grants.description: Funding for under-resourced 'Extension dioceses' in the U.S.: church and facility construction and renovation, leadership formation, young-adult and youth ministry, pastoral and social ministry, and capacity building that includes support for Catholic schools. Parishes and schools reach it only through their diocese.
grants.geography: 87 pre-approved Extension (mission) dioceses only; in Texas: Amarillo, Beaumont, Brownsville, El Paso, Laredo, Lubbock, San Angelo and Tyler (not Austin, San Antonio, Galveston-Houston, Dallas, Fort Worth, Corpus Christi or Victoria)
grants.eligibility_notes: Only requests submitted by pre-designated Extension dioceses are considered; no applications from other organizations or individuals. Requests go through the diocese's designated primary contact and must fit the diocese's strategic plan and that year's funding priorities.
focus_areas: Building Capacity (includes support for Catholic schools)

grants.grant_name: Catholic Services Appeal (CSA) Parish and School Grant Program
grants.deadline_notes: Not a written application: during each year's Catholic Services Appeal, parishes and schools earn drawing tickets for meeting appeal milestones, and winning tickets are drawn at a CSA reception each October. Rules for the current appeal are on the diocese's CSA grant program page (austindiocese.org/csa-grant-program).
grants.amount: Varies (earlier cycles: $2,500 - $10,000 per winner)
grants.typical_award: 2022 drawing: 16 parishes won grants such as $5,000 and $2,500; one deanery received $10,000 (diocesan magazine)
grants.description: Diocesan incentive grants for parish operations and tuition assistance, awarded to parishes, deaneries and Catholic schools that reach Catholic Services Appeal milestones. Past winners used awards for school security film, air-conditioning repairs and a deanery-wide formation event.
grants.geography: Diocese of Austin parishes, missions and Catholic schools only
grants.eligibility_notes: Automatically open to parishes and schools of the Diocese of Austin through their CSA participation. The diocese's own program page blocks automated checks, so current milestones, ticket rules and the total pool are unconfirmed here; earlier cycles awarded $150,000 in total.
focus_areas: Rewarding parish participation in the Catholic Services Appeal

grants.deadline_notes: A Call for Letters of Intent (500-word pitch) opens every fall on the CommunityForce portal; selected applicants are invited to a full application. Exact dates for the current cycle are not posted - subscribe to the CHRISTUS Fund newsletter. Late submissions are not accepted.
grants.typical_award: 2024 cycle: more than $3.3 million to 47 nonprofits (about $70,000 average; CHRISTUS announcement)
grants.description: Catholic health system fund for one-year programs led by local nonprofits in the primary service areas of CHRISTUS hospitals, addressing needs in its community health needs assessment. 2026-2028 priorities run by life stage, including school-age children and adolescent health.
grants.geography: Primary service areas of CHRISTUS Health hospitals in Texas, Louisiana and New Mexico (e.g. Southeast Texas); check whether your area is in a CHRISTUS hospital's primary service area
grants.eligibility_notes: Lead applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that is not a private foundation (or use a fiscal sponsor); collaboratives may include school districts and local governments. No capital or construction, endowments, event sponsorships, grants or scholarships to individuals, or indirect costs above 15%. Churches and private schools are not addressed - confirm by email through the website.
focus_areas: Adult health (access to care, healthy foods, behavioral health, chronic disease, housing)

grants.grant_name: CNAMB and BCIM School and Religious Education Program Grants
grants.funder: Black and Indian Mission Office (Catholic Negro-American Mission Board / Bureau of Catholic Indian Missions)
grants.deadline_notes: Annual calendar-year grants; applications for the January 1 - December 31, 2027 grant year are already closed. Watch the website for the 2028 application window.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: Grants to Catholic schools and parish or school religious education programs serving African American (CNAMB) or Native American/Alaska Native (BCIM) Catholic communities. School grants help with teacher salaries; religious education grants cover catechist stipends, catechetical materials and Bibles.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: Schools and religious education programs that support Catholic African American or Native American/Alaska Native communities. Amounts are not published.
focus_areas: Evangelization of African American, Native American and Alaska Native communities
Teacher salaries in Catholic schools serving these communities
Catechist stipends, catechetical materials and Bibles

grants.deadline_notes: Letter of Intent for the Spring 2027 cycle is due Friday, November 13, 2026 (LOI window opened September 1). Approved LOIs are invited to a full application, followed by a trustee site visit; the process takes about two months. A fall cycle also runs each year; its LOI date is posted later.
grants.typical_award: Spring 2026 cycle: $1.55 million to 37 recipients (about $42,000 average; foundation announcement)
grants.description: Twice-yearly grants from the foundation's Philanthropy Fund and donor endowments to Catholic churches, Catholic schools and Catholic-serving nonprofits in the Diocese of Dallas. Recent awards funded security systems, roofs, HVAC, technology, parish hall renovations and tuition assistance.
grants.geography: Diocese of Dallas only (not open to Diocese of Austin parishes or schools)
grants.eligibility_notes: Catholic organizations in the Diocese of Dallas; churches and schools apply separately. One project per request, used within one year. No operating expenses (salaries, marketing, maintenance), endowments, events, debt or reimbursement of completed projects. Grantees wait two years before reapplying.
focus_areas: Projects that would not be possible without the Foundation's support
Projects that continue after the grant and become self-supporting
Facility, safety and technology improvements for Catholic churches and schools

grants.funder: CommonSpirit Health (CHI St. Joseph Health and CHI St. Luke's Health hospitals in Texas)
grants.deadline_notes: Annual cycle: the 2027 grant round accepted applications July 20 - September 18, 2026 (now closed); decisions about January 20, 2027 for projects April 2027 - March 2028. Expect the next window around July-September 2027.
grants.amount: Small grants up to $19,500; standard grants $20,000 - $150,000 (each hospital sets its own range; Texas hospitals $6,500 - $150,000)
grants.description: Catholic health system grants for 9-12 month projects that address needs in a participating hospital's community health needs assessment. Texas participants include CHI St. Joseph Health (Bryan/College Station, Caldwell, Navasota, Madisonville) and CHI St. Luke's Health (Houston, Sugar Land, The Woodlands, Lake Jackson, Lufkin/Livingston/San Augustine).
grants.geography: Service areas of participating CommonSpirit hospitals; in Texas: Brazos Valley (Bryan/College Station, Caldwell, Navasota, Madisonville) and Greater Houston/East Texas St. Luke's hospitals
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) with an IRS determination letter (or a 501(c)(3) fiscal agent) whose services are consistent with CommonSpirit's mission; must serve the community at large including underserved people. Grants of $20,000+ need two or more collaborating partners. No capital projects, unrestricted operating support, event sponsorships or lobbying. Religious applicants are not addressed - confirm with the local grant leader.
focus_areas: Social determinants of health / health equity

grants.grant_name: Faith and AI Rapid Response Grants and Impact Grants (DELTA Partner Program)
grants.funder: University of Notre Dame Institute for Ethics and the Common Good (DELTA Network, supported by Lilly Endowment Inc.)
grants.deadline_notes: The Rapid Response round (up to $100,000 for April - September 2026 projects) is closed. Notre Dame says a second phase of two-year Impact Grants ($500,000 - $1 million) comes next and will be open to new applicants; no date has been posted.
grants.amount: Rapid Response: up to $100,000 (closed); Impact Grants: $500,000 - $1,000,000 (next phase)
grants.typical_award: 2026 Rapid Response round: more than $800,000 across 12 grantees
grants.description: Funds organizations, including K-12 schools and parishes, to build practical tools on the ethical and spiritual sides of AI, rooted in the Christian DELTA framework (Dignity, Embodiment, Love, Transcendence, Agency). Examples include a K-8 curriculum, teacher PD, parent formation guides or pastoral training. Grantees join a community of practice and present at Notre Dame's Summit on AI, Faith, and Human Flourishing.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: Open to religious organizations, K-12 and higher-education institutions, and others working where AI, ethics and faith meet; a Principal Investigator must attend the Notre Dame summit and work on a community-of-practice team. Rapid Response grants paid no indirect costs. 2026 grantees included Catholic and Christian schools and a parish.
focus_areas: K-8 curriculum, resources or PD on ethical AI use grounded in the DELTA framework
High school curriculum on ethical AI use
Pastoral training on AI for Christian communities

grants.funder: The John G. and Marie Stella Kenedy Memorial Foundation
grants.deadline_notes: 'OCTOBER 15th ANNUAL DEADLINE' - applications received by October 15th are considered at the May Board meeting. Today (October 15, 2026) is the deadline for the May 2027 decisions; the next one is October 15, 2027. Few exceptions; emergency relief requests may be considered outside the cycle.
grants.amount: Varies; sectarian requests over $50,000 (non-sectarian over $25,000) need a three-fourths Board vote; fundraising-event support generally capped at $5,000
grants.description: Funds Catholic and non-sectarian charities in Texas only. Nearly 90% of giving goes to Catholic entities, mainly schools and churches; about 70% of discretionary Catholic grants go to South Texas and the rest to other Texas dioceses. Catholic education is its number one priority, including tuition assistance for South Texas Catholic schools and for Texas Catholic schools with demonstrated need.
grants.geography: Texas only (about 70% of discretionary Catholic grants go to South Texas)
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) listed in IRS Publication 78 or the Official Catholic Directory; Texas organizations only. Apply online after passing the Eligibility Quiz; Catholic applicants should first check their diocese's protocol. A parish school applies separately from its parish; one application per organization every 12 months. Not funded: completed projects, debts or deficits, political activity or lobbying, scholarships or grants to individuals; endowments disfavored. Required uploads (Exhibits A-H) include the IRS letter or Official Catholic Directory page, board list and minutes, funding summary, detailed budget, financial statements, Form 990 and a litigation disclosure. Grants over $5,000 require a final Grant Status Report. Do not lobby Board members.
focus_areas: Catholic education (the foundation's number one priority)
Tuition assistance for Catholic schools in South Texas and schools with demonstrated need elsewhere in Texas
Breaking the cycle of poverty; helping people help themselves
Developing the Catholic faith and supporting Catholic institutions
Seed money for projects with lasting effects

grants.deadline_notes: Letters of Request are accepted January 1 - May 1 each year (next window opens January 1, 2027). Invited applicants must complete the full application within 90 days of the invitation letter; the Board decides at its annual meeting on the last Saturday in February of the following year and notifies applicants by the end of March.
grants.amount: Varies: awards have ranged from $500 to $1,000,000; one-year funding only
grants.typical_award: Average award around $10,000 (Koch FAQ); 2025: 318 grants totaling $6,327,450
grants.description: Funds Catholic evangelization in the U.S. and worldwide, including Catholic schools as a means of evangelization, catechesis and formation of evangelists, Catholic media, and renovation of Church facilities in the U.S. Priority goes to sound but financially needy programs in distressed or underdeveloped regions.
grants.geography: National (international funder, no geographic preference)
grants.eligibility_notes: Catholic non-profits recognized by the Holy See and engaged in evangelization; U.S. applicants must be listed in the Official Catholic Directory and/or hold an IRS exemption letter. One request per cycle per parish, school or organization; no more than 3 grants in any 5-year period. U.S. capital projects over $50,000 need at least 50% secured from other sources plus a signed construction proposal. Not funded: multi-year commitments, endowments, capital campaigns, debt, vehicles, land or building purchases, tuition or individual grants, marketing campaigns, projects completed before the February meeting, general healthcare or social services.

grants.deadline_notes: No fixed deadline published; participation usually starts when a pastor identifies families in his parish and enrolls them through the program, before the school year. Contact the program through its website.
grants.amount: Varies (supplemental tuition payments)
grants.typical_award: 2022-23: more than 260 children from about 175 families at 12 of the diocese's 20 Catholic schools (diocesan magazine)
grants.description: Catholic nonprofit, approved diocese-wide by the Bishop of Austin, that helps the poorest families in Diocese of Austin parishes send children to Catholic elementary and high schools. Participating schools discount tuition, the sponsoring parish pays part with supplemental payments from Our Kids at Heart, and families pay what they can.
grants.geography: Diocese of Austin (chapters in Austin, Bryan, Waco and Temple)
grants.eligibility_notes: Open to youth in all parishes of the diocese; families must show financial need through an independent review and attend Mass regularly as a family. Requires a sponsoring parish and a participating Catholic school; parish enrollment steps are not published online.
focus_areas: Barrier-free Catholic education for economically disadvantaged families

grants.grant_name: Raskob Foundation for Catholic Activities Grants
grants.deadline_notes: Domestic Spring cycle: submit January 1-15 (5 pm ET), decision end of May. Domestic Fall cycle: submit June 1-15, decision end of November. International cycle May 1-15. Online portal only, in English.
grants.amount: Varies (no published range)
grants.typical_award: 2025 domestic grants: median $25,000; middle half $15,000 - $30,000; largest $85,000 (138 grants, 2025 Grants Approved Report)
grants.description: Family foundation serving the Catholic Church and organizations identified with it. Domestic grants support projects of U.S. Catholic organizations such as dioceses, schools, religious communities and Catholic charities, including education, social services, health and ministry programs and some construction.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: U.S. applicants must be 501(c)(3) public charities listed in the Official Catholic Directory and include a signed letter on letterhead from the bishop (or a provincial or religious congregational leader). Construction/renovation over $200,000 is eligible only after 50% of cost is in hand, a construction contract is signed and work is underway. Not funded: requests by or for individuals (tuition, scholarships), endowments, debt reduction, anything completed before the Board meets, lobbying.
focus_areas: Projects of Catholic organizations in the U.S. and territories (Domestic Program)
Program and operating expenses of Catholic ministries, schools and charities
Construction or renovation (projects over $200,000 only once conditions are met)

grants.deadline_notes: Session 2027A: opens November 1, due December 15, 2026, decision by June 1. Session 2027B: opens May 1, due June 15, 2027, decision by December 1. Late applications are not accepted.
grants.amount: Applicants may request any amount; the board may approve all or part
grants.description: Houston-based foundation that furthers the Roman Catholic faith in Texas by funding Catholic religious, charitable and educational institutions across the state's fifteen dioceses, guided by a 25-year strategic plan built on a culture of vocations.
grants.geography: Texas only
grants.eligibility_notes: Roman Catholic 501(c)(3) organizations in Texas; no individuals. One unsolicited application per organization per calendar year (dioceses may submit two). Apply by email with the funder's PDF forms; no matching grants. High schools outside the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston receive Scanlan Scholars tuition aid through their diocese, not by applying.
focus_areas: A culture of vocations to the priesthood, religious life and holy families

grants.deadline_notes: The 2026 application form states there are no deadlines; the board generally meets three times a year, in February, July and November. Email the completed application and attachments as one PDF.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: Houston-based Catholic family foundation that supports Catholic causes guided by traditional Catholic values. Catholic institutions are its first donor-intent priority, so Catholic parishes and schools in Texas fit its guidelines.
grants.geography: Texas focus (Houston priority for poverty and civic/cultural grants, with secondary consideration for Austin, Dallas and the rest of Texas)
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) organizations only; no grants to individuals. Its education priority names private secondary and higher education, so a K-8 request is better framed under the Catholic-institution priority. Attach the IRS determination letter, most recent 990, board list and list of other contributors.
focus_areas: Judeo-Christian religious organizations, with priority to Catholic institutions
Hospitals and medical research (women's health, pro-life)
Private secondary and higher education aligned with Catholic institutions

grants.funder: Diocese of Austin Women's Giving Circle (endowment at the Catholic Foundation - Diocese of Austin)
grants.deadline_notes: By invitation: a grant committee invites Catholic-aligned nonprofits to apply, finalists present at a spring gathering, and members vote; 2026 awards were presented June 20, 2026. Registration for the next cycle reopens in fall 2026.
grants.description: Giving circle of Catholic women, launched by the Diocese of Austin in fall 2025, that pools annual dues to fund Catholic-aligned organizations in Central Texas. First-year recipients included a Catholic school, a parish food pantry and a campus ministry.
grants.geography: Central Texas / Diocese of Austin
grants.eligibility_notes: Catholic-aligned nonprofits serving Central Texas, including parishes and Catholic schools; organizations must be invited by the grant committee to apply.
focus_areas: Food access, family and youth services, Catholic education

grants.funder: USCCB Subcommittee on Catholic Home Missions
grants.deadline_notes: The online application opens in early January each year and all diocesan applications must be received by April 1; the Subcommittee decides in October, notifies by mid-November and pays semi-annually from January.
grants.amount: No minimum; maximum $125,000 per (arch)diocese
grants.typical_award: 2025-2026: more than $7.8 million to 69 dioceses and eparchies (about $113,000 per diocese on average)
grants.description: Operating support for evangelization, catechesis, parish life and ministry training in U.S. home mission dioceses. Funds go to the diocese, which supports its parishes and ministries.
grants.geography: Home mission dioceses and eparchies only (2025 Texas recipient: Diocese of Brownsville)
grants.eligibility_notes: Currently only Class I applicants (diocesan bishops of home mission dioceses) are approved; parishes and schools cannot apply directly. Every application needs the bishop's signature and endorsement and audited financial statements. Covers operating expenses; ordinarily no capital expenses, endowments or loans; exclusively social-service programs should look elsewhere.
focus_areas: Promotion of parish life and support of poor parishes
Training of priests, deacons, religious and lay ministers

grants.grant_name: CorWorks Parish Innovation Grants (OSV Institute for Catholic Innovation)
grants.deadline_notes: Cohort 2 applications open October 9 and close November 20, 2026; interviews November 23 - December 11; decisions by December 11, 2026; training retreat January 25-29, 2027, then a 90-day challenge through April 18, 2027. At most 6 parishes per cohort.
grants.amount: Up to $25,000 in seed funding, plus retreat travel, lodging, meals and training covered by OSV
grants.description: A parish innovation program: a 3-4 person parish team attends a week-long retreat, designs a response to a specific local need rooted in the Corporal Works of Mercy, and launches it in a 90-day challenge with coaching. Participating parishes may receive up to $25,000 in seed funding.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: Any Catholic parish whose pastor actively supports participation and can field a team of 3-4 committed people; no minimum parish size. Needs a clearly defined local problem and evidence of firsthand pre-work. No program fee; a $2,500 refundable deposit is due at acceptance. Schools are not the applicant; the parish team is.
focus_areas: Parish response to a specific, evidenced local need
Catholic innovation (design thinking, prototyping, community listening)

grants.grant_name: Friends of the Poor Grant Program
grants.funder: Society of St. Vincent de Paul USA (National Council)
grants.deadline_notes: Three rounds a year; each region (Texas is in the South Central region) gets one submission window per fiscal year, posted on the program page. Early or late applications are not considered. Decisions come about six weeks after the deadline. An informational webinar is set for October 23, 2026.
grants.amount: Up to $5,000
grants.typical_award: FY2025-26: $420,000 shared by 92 Conferences (about $4,600 average); about 25% of applicants funded
grants.description: Grants to local St. Vincent de Paul Conferences (usually based in a parish) for six months of direct aid to neighbors in urgent need, focused on keeping families housed. For 2026-27 the National Council raised its combined Friends of the Poor and Systemic Change commitment to $900,000.
grants.geography: National (apply in your region's window)
grants.eligibility_notes: Only Society of St. Vincent de Paul Conferences may apply: officially recognized, prior-year annual report filed, solidarity contribution paid, and in good standing as a 501(c)(3). A parish without an SVdP Conference cannot apply. Grantees wait two fiscal years before reapplying. No building projects or staff costs.
focus_areas: Food, clothing, medical and transportation needs

grants.funder: Diocese of Austin (Rural Parish Endowment, Catholic Foundation - Diocese of Austin)
grants.deadline_notes: Distributed by the diocese from a $1 million endowment created by the Encountering Christ campaign; no public application window or form was found. Ask the diocesan Stewardship and Development Office.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: Grants for operational and emergency support to the roughly 50 rural parishes and missions of the Diocese of Austin.
grants.geography: Rural parishes and missions of the Diocese of Austin only
grants.eligibility_notes: Rural parishes and missions only; urban parishes and schools are not eligible. Application process, amounts and timing are unconfirmed.
focus_areas: Emergency support for rural parishes and missions

grants.funder: Society of St. Vincent de Paul USA (National Council)
grants.deadline_notes: The next Systemic Change grant cycle begins in spring 2027; the exact deadline will be posted. Late entries are not accepted.
grants.description: One-year grants to St. Vincent de Paul Conferences and Councils for projects that address root causes of poverty (for example Getting Ahead classes, weatherization or housing programs), scored on engagement of people with lived experience, sustainability, replicability and innovation.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: Aggregated Conferences and instituted District/Diocesan Councils in 501(c)(3) compliance, current on solidarity contribution and annual report. Not for transactional aid such as rent or utilities. 2026 recipients cannot reapply for the same program this year.
focus_areas: Removing the conditions that hold poverty in place

grants.grant_name: A. M. Pate Jr. Charitable Trust Grants
grants.funder: A. M. Pate Jr. Charitable Trust (Bank of America, trustee)
grants.deadline_notes: One application deadline per year, March 1, through the Bank of America Philanthropic Solutions online application.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.typical_award: Average award $10,000 - $15,000 per grant cycle
grants.description: Texas charitable trust supporting organizations operated for religious, charitable, educational or historic-preservation purposes anywhere in Texas. Summer reading programs for Pre-K-12 readers

grants.grant_name: ESSA Title I, Part A Equitable Services for Private School Students
grants.funder: U.S. Department of Education via the Texas Education Agency and the local public school district
grants.deadline_notes: Not a competitive grant: the public school district where the private school is located must invite eligible private nonprofit schools each year (Title I, Part A outreach also reaches schools outside district lines). Consultation must happen BEFORE the district decides how to spend the next year's funds, so it is usually held in spring (Austin ISD's 2026-27 initial consultation ran May 8 - June 18, 2026; attendance at a session was required to participate). Expect the 2027-28 window around spring 2027; watch for the district's outreach letter and intent-to-participate deadline. The district must upload the signed Affirmation of Consultation to TEA by September 30 each year.
grants.amount: Varies (the private school students' equitable share of the district's Title I allocation)
grants.description: Federally funded supplemental instruction (for example tutoring, reading/math intervention, counseling, parent engagement and related teacher training) provided by the public school district to low-achieving students at a private school who live in a participating Title I public school attendance area.
grants.geography: National program; in Texas handled by the district(s) where students live, overseen by TEA
grants.eligibility_notes: Title I eligibility follows where the CHILD LIVES (a participating Title I attendance area) plus educational need, so several districts may serve one private school (they may pool funds). Funds may not be paid to the private school directly, pay substitutes for private school teachers, or cover repairs, remodeling or construction. Private NONPROFIT schools only. The school official must attend the district's consultation meetings, supply the data the district asks for, sign the Affirmation of Consultation, and help plan services. Services, not cash: the district stays the fiscal agent, hires/oversees staff and keeps title to materials and equipment, and all services must be secular, neutral and non-ideological. If the district does not consult meaningfully, the school may complain to the TEA private nonprofit school ombudsman.
focus_areas: Low-achieving students living in Title I attendance areas
Professional development tied to Title I services

focus_areas: Professional development for private school teachers and leaders
