grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) nonprofits (or fiscal sponsor) and schools listed by the National Center for Education Statistics (a private school should confirm it appears in NCES's private school listings before applying). Honda primarily funds organizations with operating budgets over $500,000. Excludes programs organized or implemented for religious purposes, athletic teams, individuals and completed programs/events; requests mainly to sponsor a single team, competition or event are not priorities.
focus_areas: Clean energy awareness and education; urban forestry; natural resource conservation

grants.grant_name: IDEA Part B Equitable Services for Parentally Placed Private School Children with Disabilities
grants.funder: U.S. Department of Education (IDEA) via the Texas Education Agency and the local public school district
grants.deadline_notes: Child Find referrals and evaluation requests can be made any time (the district must finish an initial evaluation within 45 school days of parental consent). The menu of services funded with the district's proportionate share is set through annual consultation with private school representatives and parents, so ask the district when its consultation meeting is held.
grants.amount: Varies (the district's IDEA Part B 'proportionate share' for parentally placed private school children)
grants.description: The public school district where the private school is located must locate, evaluate and identify students with disabilities enrolled in private schools (Child Find) and spend a proportionate share of its federal IDEA funds on special education and related services for them, documented in an individual services plan.
grants.geography: National program; in Texas handled by the district where the private school is located
grants.eligibility_notes: Texas (19 TAC 89.1096) defines eligible private schools to include religious schools that are nonprofit and follow an adopted curriculum. Students have no individual entitlement to the full services they would get in public school; the district decides which services it offers after consultation, and the location of services is set in consultation. Services must be secular, neutral and non-ideological.
focus_areas: Child Find (locating and evaluating students with disabilities)
Special education and related services via services plans
Proportionate share of IDEA Part B funds

grants.grant_name: Impact Austin Grants (Community, Education, Health & Well-Being)
grants.deadline_notes: Annual cycle: in 2026 applications opened January 8 and closed February 5, with site visits in April and member voting at the June annual meeting. The 2027 dates are not yet posted; a nonprofit workshop usually precedes the opening in early January.
grants.amount: Set each year by membership level (2026: $80,000 and $20,000 per focus area)
grants.typical_award: 2026: $80,000 to the top finalist and $20,000 to the runner-up in each of three focus areas
grants.description: Women's collective giving organization that awards large unrestricted grants voted on by its members, in Education, Community and Health & Well-Being. A Catholic school could apply in Education for a program serving a broad community.
grants.geography: Bastrop, Hays, Travis and Williamson counties
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) public charity providing services in the four counties; one focus area per cycle. Not eligible: sectarian or religious organizations where the grant would principally benefit their own members or adherents or fund inherently religious activities. Impact Austin's 2026 workshop slides list 'overtly religious missions' as a reviewer concern, so emphasize broad community benefit.
focus_areas: Community: economic, social, environmental or cultural initiatives
Health and well-being of children and families

grants.grant_name: Inclusive Classroom Fund Grant (plus free classroom crowdfunding page)
grants.deadline_notes: 2026 Inclusive Classroom Fund applications opened October 5 in the Teacher Dashboard and are due November 2, 2026; all applicants are notified December 4, 2026. The crowdfunding Classroom Page itself is open year-round, and donated funds can be spent for up to one year.
grants.amount: $500 per grant (at least 50 grants in the 2026 round); crowdfunding totals vary
grants.typical_award: $500 per grant (fixed amount, 2026 Inclusive Classroom Fund)
grants.description: Free crowdfunding platform where PreK-12 teachers create a Classroom Page, donors give, and teachers spend the money on supplies through the AdoptAClassroom.org Marketplace. Registered teachers can also apply for periodic classroom grants, such as the $500 Inclusive Classroom Fund for resources that serve students with IEPs, English learners and students facing social or economic marginalization.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: Licensed PreK-12 teachers or certified staff at a public, charter, or ACCREDITED private PreK-12 school in the US (an accredited Catholic school counts as an accredited private school). Teacher must register and have a Classroom Page. For the grant, high-needs schools (share of students on free/reduced lunch, with IEPs, or English learners) are prioritized; only a small number of applications from other schools are evaluated. Free for teachers; no fees on donations.
focus_areas: Students facing social or economic marginalization

grants.deadline_notes: Applications are reviewed quarterly, with deadlines March 31, June 30, September 30 and December 31. Grantees have one year from the application date to raise their matching funds.
grants.amount: Varies; covers up to 50% of the cost of quality stringed instruments (violins, violas, cellos, basses; also ukuleles and guitars)
grants.description: Matching grants that help K-12 string and orchestra programs buy quality instruments through the foundation's authorized instrument provider, encouraging local fundraising for music education.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: Applicant (or partner) must have nonprofit status (IRS determination letter) and serve children in grades K-12; grants are not made to individuals. Must show need and a plan to raise matching funds; two letters of support required. No public-only or religious exclusion is stated in the application.
focus_areas: String instrument programs for K-12 students
Quality instruments for school and community music programs

grants.grant_name: INVITE AI in K12 Teacher Fellowship Program
grants.funder: INVITE AI Institute, University of Illinois (funded by NSF and the Institute of Education Sciences)
grants.deadline_notes: The 2026 round closed March 17, 2026; fellows attended the CSTA Annual Conference (July 13-15, 2026), a fall webinar and ran a fall classroom pilot. No 2027 call has been posted.
grants.amount: Free CSTA Annual Conference registration plus a $1,500 travel stipend
grants.typical_award: $1,500 travel stipend plus registration
grants.description: Helps K-12 teachers of any subject bring fair, inclusive AI learning into class. Fellows attend AI-in-K12 workshops at the national CSTA conference, join a follow-up webinar, try an AI lesson or activity with at least one class, and write a reflection.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: K-12 teachers in any subject (no public/private restriction stated). Fellows commit to at least 3 AI sessions at the conference, a fall webinar, one classroom pilot and a written reflection.
focus_areas: Equitable and inclusive AI learning experiences

grants.funder: Joni Elaine Templeton Foundation (Bank of America, trustee)
grants.deadline_notes: One application deadline per year, May 1, through the Bank of America Philanthropic Solutions online application.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.typical_award: Average award about $5,000 per grant cycle
grants.description: Small private foundation managed by Bank of America that gives preference to organizations operating in or serving Austin, Texas. Its purposes explicitly include religious and educational work, so an Austin parish or Catholic school can apply.
grants.geography: Texas, with preference for organizations operating in or serving Austin
grants.eligibility_notes: Qualified 501(c)(3) charitable organizations. Listed program types include Religion-Related, Education, Human Services, Community Improvement and Animal-Related.
focus_areas: Prevention of cruelty to children or animals

grants.deadline_notes: No deadline; applications are taken only from the cities or metro areas KABOOM! currently lists, and it advises others not to apply now. The list changes, so check the page regularly.
grants.amount: Varies (playspace built with a KABOOM! funding partner)
grants.description: KABOOM! and a funding partner plan, design and build a new community playground, nature exploration area, multi-sport court or adventure course with the community. It partners with child-serving nonprofits and municipal agencies.
grants.geography: Listed metro areas only; in Texas: Dallas, Fort Worth, Houston and San Antonio (not Austin as of October 2026)
grants.eligibility_notes: Builds in partnership with child-serving nonprofits and municipal agencies; eligibility is confirmed through an eligibility quiz and screening. The site does not say whether religious schools or churches qualify. A separate Georgia Playspace Refresh Fund (up to $25,000) is for Georgia only.

grants.grant_name: Katherine C. Carmody Charitable Trust Grants
grants.funder: Katherine C. Carmody Charitable Trust (Bank of America, trustee)
grants.deadline_notes: One application deadline per year, August 1. Grantees must skip two years before reapplying.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: Texas trust that limits grants to 501(c)(3) organizations in Texas operated exclusively for religious, charitable or educational purposes. Preference goes to Navarro County and the Dallas area, but any Texas organization may apply.
grants.geography: Texas (preference for Navarro County and the Dallas area)
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) organizations within Texas operated exclusively for religious, charitable or educational purposes; two-year wait after a grant.

grants.grant_name: Launch K-8 Computer Science (Launch_K5 CS and Launch Middle School CS) teacher trainings and Train-the-Trainer
grants.funder: WeTeach_CS, Texas Advanced Computing Center, The University of Texas at Austin
grants.deadline_notes: Free workshops are scheduled through the year by education service center region; fall 2026 sessions include Region 13 at TCEA on October 20-21, 2026. Certified trainers earn $3,000 for training at least 30 educators by the end of August 2027.
grants.amount: Free training plus up to $200 in physical computing kits per teacher; $3,000 per certified trainer
grants.typical_award: Up to $200 of classroom kits per teacher
grants.description: Free 2-3 day hybrid workshops that help K-5 teachers, and since spring 2026 grades 6-8 teachers, build computational thinking, computer science, cybersecurity and AI into core subjects and meet the Technology Applications TEKS. Each teacher keeps a physical computing kit. A teacher or school can also become a certified trainer and earn $3,000 for training 30 or more educators. This is free training and equipment, not a cash grant.
grants.geography: Texas (workshops held by education service center region, including Region 13)
grants.eligibility_notes: Workshops are free and open to any Texas educator who is interested; the statewide trainings require working at a Texas school that serves K-5 (or grades 6-8 for the middle school version). Trainer pay goes to the individual or the school.
focus_areas: Integrating the Technology Applications TEKS into K-8 core curricula
Computational thinking, computer science, cybersecurity and AI

grants.grant_name: Laura Bush Foundation for America's Libraries
grants.funder: Laura Bush Foundation for America's Libraries (George W. Bush Presidential Center)
grants.deadline_notes: Applications for the 2026 grant are due Thursday, December 31, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. CT; awardees are notified in spring 2027 and must spend funds by December 31, 2027. The foundation says 2027 will mark the final round of LBF grants.
grants.amount: Not stated by funder; 2026 awardees reported $5,000 grants
grants.typical_award: $5,000 per school reported in 2026 (220 school libraries shared $1 million)
grants.description: Grants to update and expand school library book collections at low-income schools. Private and parochial schools are eligible if at least half of their students qualify for financial aid.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: Private and parochial schools: at least 50% of students must qualify for financial aid (public schools must be Title I eligible). Needs a library or designated space where all students can check out books, and a paid school or district employee responsible for the collection. Funds only books and subscriptions: no shelving, furniture, equipment, staffing, software, videos or tests.
focus_areas: School library books for low-income schools

grants.deadline_notes: Two rounds a year: applications open online January 1 and July 1 and are due by midnight January 31 and July 31 (not extended). Review takes up to 10 weeks; projects must be finished within 12 months of funding.
grants.amount: Up to $100,000 (most $25,000 or less; several up to $50,000; one up to $100,000 per round)
grants.typical_award: Most grants are $25,000 or less; FY2026: 81 grants totaling $2,177,486
grants.description: Capital improvement grants for community projects in LCRA's wholesale power, water and transmission service areas. A parish or school could use it for a community-use facility upgrade such as energy-efficient lighting, solar or water conservation if the facility is genuinely open to the whole community.
grants.geography: LCRA service area: all or part of 73 Texas counties, including Travis, Williamson, Hays, Bastrop, Burnet, Caldwell, Blanco and Llano (project must have a physical address in the service area)
grants.eligibility_notes: Tax-exempt nonprofits, local governments, schools and hospitals. Religious sanctuaries are not eligible, and projects must benefit or be available to an entire community. Not for social service or limited-use facilities, operating costs, furniture, computers or office equipment. 20% cash or in-kind match for projects over $5,000; no LCRA grant in the past 24 months.
focus_areas: Capital improvements serving the whole community
Water and energy conservation features (xeriscaping, rainwater catchment, solar, LED lighting)

grants.deadline_notes: Two deadlines a year: February 28 (May board meeting) and August 31 (November board meeting); applications must be received, not just postmarked, by the deadline (prior working day if it falls on a weekend or holiday). Decisions in three to four months.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: Austin-area private foundation (Bank of America, agent) supporting community-based organizations within about 50 miles of Austin. Funding emphases include early childhood and youth development, so a defined school or parish youth project or equipment request fits.
grants.geography: Seven Central Texas counties: Bastrop, Blanco, Burnet, Caldwell, Hays, Travis and Williamson
grants.eligibility_notes: Must be a qualified public charity under 501(c)(3); generally does not fund day-to-day operating costs; one grant per 12 months; final report required. The guidelines do not mention religious organizations.

grants.deadline_notes: No fixed deadline; one proposal per organization every 12 months. The board meets in January, April, June, September and November, and review takes 4-5 months, so apply at least four months before funds are needed.
grants.amount: Varies (no published range)
grants.description: Foundation supporting Texas nonprofits and public entities in arts and culture, civic and public affairs, education, environment, health and human services. About 85% of giving supports specific programs or projects; capital projects are a small share.
grants.geography: Texas (up to 50% of giving in Dallas-Fort Worth)
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) public charities or public entities whose work benefits Texas. The guidelines neither include nor exclude religious organizations or private schools. Not funded: fundraising events, annual drives, scholarships, out-of-state travel, single performances, conferences outside its initiative areas; endowment grants are rare.
focus_areas: Arts & culture and civic & public affairs

grants.grant_name: Middle School CS Scholarship (Tech and Play: CS Workshops for Middle School Teachers)
grants.funder: UTeach Computer Science, The University of Texas at Austin (funded by WeTeach_CS and Lockheed Martin)
grants.deadline_notes: 2026 workshops ran June 1-4 (Arlington), July 20-23 (San Antonio) and July 28-31 (Austin), with applications reviewed on a rolling basis (Austin: apply by July 1, 2026). 2027 dates have not been posted.
grants.amount: $800 stipend plus free PD (valued at $1,000) and a STEM kit (valued at $1,100)
grants.typical_award: $800 stipend per teacher
grants.description: Scholarships for Texas middle school teachers to attend a free four-day workshop: 'vibe coding' in Scratch with AI as a co-pilot, Sphero robotics, and solar-powered engineering, with 28 CPE hours. Teachers keep a full STEM kit with robots, Technology Applications curriculum and platform accounts.
grants.geography: Texas (2026 workshops in Austin, San Antonio and Arlington)
grants.eligibility_notes: Must teach at a Texas middle school in the coming school year and attend a whole workshop; preference to teachers scheduled to teach CS or Technology Applications. No public-school-only rule is stated; grade 6-8 teachers at a K-8 school should confirm they count. Participants pay their own travel, lodging and dinners.
focus_areas: Scratch coding with AI as a co-pilot
Integrating STEM tools and AI into daily lessons

grants.deadline_notes: Grant inquiries are accepted year-round through the online portal (eligibility quiz, then a short inquiry); invited applicants complete a full application that goes to one of four trustee meetings a year. Inquiry to decision can take up to 12 months. One active grant per organization.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.typical_award: Grants to Catholic schools in the foundation's online grants database range from about $10,000 to $250,000 (2018-2026)
grants.description: Major Texas foundation that funds projects statewide, with a key focus on Galveston, Austin and Dallas and special attention to rural areas. Its grants database shows past awards to Catholic schools, including an Austin-area Catholic school for early literacy and a Catholic school building project.
grants.geography: Texas (all funds must be spent in Texas; key focus on Galveston, Austin and Dallas)
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) public charity (or government entity, certain 509(a)(3) supporting organizations, private operating foundations). Prefers program or project grants; will consider operating support and occasionally capital. Scholarships go only through the separate Moody Scholars program. The Education M-Pact Fund is a separate, currently invitation-only rural cycle.

grants.grant_name: Music Education & Community Program Grant (Music License Plate Grant)
grants.funder: Texas Music Office, Office of the Texas Governor
grants.deadline_notes: FY2027 funding opportunity opened October 5, 2026 in the Governor's eGrants system and is due December 7, 2026. Project period up to 12 months.
grants.description: Small state grants, funded by Texas music specialty license plate sales, for music education and community music programs sponsored by Texas-based nonprofits. A school music program or parish community music project fits.
grants.geography: Texas
grants.eligibility_notes: Only Texas-based 501(c)(3) nonprofits; must be organized and based in Texas, in good standing with the State of Texas and owe no delinquent Texas taxes. Apply in eGrants. The guidelines do not address religious organizations; expect state funds to support only non-religious music education.

grants.deadline_notes: Two-stage process: the online initial inquiry form is open June 15 - January 15; selected applicants are invited in March to submit full proposals in April; decisions are announced around mid-June. Small instrument/equipment requests ($2,000 or less) get a separate February review.
grants.amount: $100 - $10,000 (one-time, non-renewable)
grants.description: All-volunteer foundation funded by Phish fans that supports music education for children: instruments, texts, equipment, practice/performance space and instruction, with special interest in creative expression (composition, improvisation) and diverse musical styles. It does not fund music therapy or music appreciation without participation.
grants.geography: National (U.S. only)
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) nonprofits (or fiscally sponsored programs) and government entities such as public schools; the foundation says it has funded public and private schools. Does not normally fund programs that promote or engage in religious doctrine, individuals, research or fundraising events. Highly competitive (several dozen grants a year from 1,000+ inquiries).
focus_areas: Music education for children 18 and under
Creative expression: instrumentation, voice, composition, improvisation

grants.grant_name: National School Lunch Program, School Breakfast Program and Special Milk Program (private nonprofit schools)
grants.funder: USDA Food and Nutrition Service via the Texas Department of Agriculture (Square Meals)
grants.deadline_notes: New schools can submit TDA's new-applicant form at any time; allow lead time before the school year for TDA's review and the permanent agreement. Once in NSLP, an elementary school may be invited into the Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program, which TDA runs by invitation for schools with high free/reduced-price enrollment.
grants.amount: Federal per-meal reimbursements (rates set annually) plus USDA Foods; FFVP adds $50 - $75 per student per year
grants.description: Federal reimbursement for nutritious lunches and breakfasts (and milk under the Special Milk Program) served to students, with free and reduced-price meals for eligible families. Participation also opens doors to related programs such as the Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program and USDA Farm to School grants.
grants.geography: Texas (federal program administered by TDA for Texas schools)
grants.eligibility_notes: TDA accepts a nonprofit organization that runs private schools of high school grade or under that are recognized as part of the Texas educational system, and that is not already in NSLP, SBP, CACFP or SFSP. Meals must meet federal nutrition guidelines and are reimbursed by the number of meals served; the operator signs a permanent agreement with TDA.
focus_areas: Nutritious low-cost or free school lunches and breakfasts
Free and reduced-price meals for low-income families
Fresh fruit and vegetable access in high-need elementary schools

grants.grant_name: NEH Summer Institutes and Landmarks of American History and Culture Workshops for K-12 Educators (participant stipends)
grants.deadline_notes: Teachers apply directly to individual summer programs. NEH says summer 2027 programs will be posted in early 2027, with participant application and notification dates to be announced.
grants.amount: Participant stipend: $1,600 (one week), $2,500 (two weeks) or $3,200 (three weeks)
grants.typical_award: Fixed stipends: $1,600 / $2,500 / $3,200 depending on program length
grants.description: Residential one- to three-week summer programs on humanities topics (history, literature, civics, etc.) for K-12 teachers, hosted by colleges and humanities organizations around the country. Selected teachers receive a stipend to cover travel, lodging and meals.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: Open to full- or part-time K-12 educators who teach in public, charter, independent AND religiously affiliated schools, and to home-school educators; participants must be U.S. citizens, residents of U.S. jurisdictions, or foreign nationals living in the U.S. for at least three years.

grants.funder: Office of the Texas Governor, Public Safety Office (FEMA funds)
grants.deadline_notes: Texas runs the state application in eGrants each winter: FY2026 was open January 12 - March 12, 2026 (FY2025: January 13 - March 13, 2025). The next cycle has not been posted yet. Requires an active SAM.gov registration and a vulnerability assessment; one application per site.
grants.amount: Up to $150,000 per site, up to three sites (per the Texas pre-application guide citing the FY2023 FEMA notice; FEMA sets the cap each year)
grants.description: Federal security grants passed through the Texas Office of the Governor for nonprofits at high risk of terrorist or extremist attack. Houses of worship and nonprofit educational facilities are listed as eligible, so a parish and its school can each apply as separate sites.
grants.geography: Texas. Austin-area applicants (Travis, Williamson and Hays counties) apply under the Austin urban area (NSGP-UA); the rest of Texas under NSGP-S
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) organizations (faith-based organizations may be exempted from providing proof of 501(c)(3) status), active SAM.gov registration, and a showing of high risk of attack. Public schools are not eligible. No match. Post-award environmental and historic review applies to installations.

grants.grant_name: Patrick Leahy Farm to School Grant Program
grants.deadline_notes: The FY2026 request for applications closed December 5, 2025 (posted September 10, 2025) and FY2026 awards have been announced; USDA had not posted an FY2027 request for applications as of October 15, 2026 and says requirements can change each year.
grants.amount: FY2026: $100,000 - $500,000 per award (up to $18 million total)
grants.description: Competitive grants for farm to school projects that bring local foods into school meals and teach students about agriculture, food and nutrition (school gardens, local procurement, food education).
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: FY2026 eligible applicants included Child Nutrition Program operators (a private school that runs NSLP is one), local agencies, Indian tribal organizations, agricultural producers and nonprofits (501(c)(3) letter required). Under the FY2026 notice, Child Nutrition Program operators had to apply as part of a partnership. At $100,000+, a single K-8 school is most realistic as a partner in a larger application.
focus_areas: School gardens and farm to school partnerships

grants.deadline_notes: Fall 2026 round open now through November 3, 2026 (online through PEC's Submittable form); recipients awarded in January. PEC awards community grants twice a year; funded organizations sit out one cycle.
grants.amount: Up to $5,000
grants.typical_award: March 2026 round: nearly $40,000 to nine nonprofits
grants.description: Small grants from PEC's member-funded Power of Change program for capital improvements, technology and energy-efficiency equipment at nonprofits in the PEC service area. A parish hall or school building open to the community could qualify for lighting, HVAC or similar upgrades.
grants.geography: PEC service area in the Texas Hill Country (PEC offices include Oak Hill in southwest Austin, Kyle, Liberty Hill and Marble Falls); most of the City of Austin is served by Austin Energy, so check the PEC service-area map
grants.eligibility_notes: Nonprofit organized under Texas law and in good standing with the Texas Secretary of State and Comptroller, with an IRS determination letter (a Texas sales tax exemption certificate is not accepted); not majority funded by taxing entities. Cannot fund religious or church-sponsored facilities limited to church membership, projects that exclusively serve religious purposes, operating costs, scholarships, endowments or fundraisers.

grants.grant_name: Pets in the Classroom Teacher Grants
grants.deadline_notes: For the 2026-27 school year, April 30, 2027 is the last day to apply for any grant (store coupon, rebate or sustaining); receipts are due by May 31, 2027. Approval emails go out about 14 days after applying (slower August-October).
grants.amount: Initial grant: pet-store coupons or a rebate of up to $75 (small animal/betta) or $125 (fish/amphibian/reptile); then $50 sustaining grant each later school year
grants.typical_award: $50 - $125 per grant (fixed amounts by grant type)
grants.description: Small grants that help PreK-12 teachers buy and care for a classroom pet (small mammals, birds, fish, reptiles, etc.) and its habitat, through store coupons (Petco, PetSmart, Pet Supplies Plus, Petland, Pet Supermarket) or reimbursement.
grants.geography: National (U.S., Puerto Rico and Canada)
grants.eligibility_notes: PreK-12 teachers in public AND private schools (also librarians, counselors, nurses and other school staff); grants go to the individual teacher with the principal's permission. Not for home daycares, homeschools or virtual schools. One initial grant per teacher per lifetime; no dogs, cats, insects or experiments.
focus_areas: Responsible pet care and animal welfare

grants.grant_name: Presidential SI Challenge (formerly the Presidential AI Challenge)
grants.funder: White House Task Force on SI (AI) Education; run by ORISE for the U.S. government
grants.deadline_notes: Teams must register by December 18, 2026 and submit projects by December 23, 2026 (5:00 pm ET). State champions are named by February 15, 2027, virtual regional rounds run March 4 - April 8, 2027, and the national finals are June 6-9, 2027 in Washington, DC.
grants.amount: State champions: $200 gift cards each; regional champions: $1,000 - $1,500 gift cards each plus a DC trip; national champions: $2,500 - $12,500 by category ($10,000 in the educator category)
grants.description: A national competition, not a grant, in which K-12 student teams and teams of 1-3 full-time teachers use AI (renamed 'Super Intelligence' or SI on September 29, 2026) to solve community problems. The educator category rewards new ways to teach with or about AI, or AI tools that improve school administrative work. Registered teams get free virtual mentorship and office hours, and every compliant entry gets a certificate.
grants.geography: National (Texas gets two state champions per category and track)
grants.eligibility_notes: Full-time K-12 classroom teachers in public, charter or private schools are eligible (age 21+, U.S. citizens, nationals or permanent residents). Student teams need a teacher or approved leader: K-5 teams have 1-5 students and grade 6-8 teams have 1-4. Work must be original and created after August 1, 2026, and consent and media forms are required.
focus_areas: Teaching with or about AI (SI) in K-12 classrooms
AI tools that transform school administrative workflows or policies
Student AI solutions to community challenges

grants.deadline_notes: The application is posted each fall (the foundation says the 2027 application is due late January/early February 2027; its FAQ says applications are accepted November-February and the exact date is printed on the application). Board review runs February-April; winners are emailed in early May, checks go out May-June, and funds must be spent within nine months.
grants.amount: Typically $2,500 - $10,000 (partial grants possible; no match required)
grants.typical_award: FAQ: grants typically $2,500 - $10,000; 2026 round: 25 grants of $1,000 - $10,000 from nearly 1,000 applications
grants.description: Grants to PreK-12 school libraries that serve disadvantaged children, for books that students will use again and again (central or classroom libraries), reference materials, magazine/newspaper subscriptions and book-processing fees. It does not fund books students keep, eBooks or technology, furniture, author visits, teacher professional books or hands-on kits.
grants.geography: National (U.S. and U.S. territories)
grants.eligibility_notes: Any U.S. school library serving disadvantaged youth; the foundation says grants go to public, private and experimental schools, and Catholic schools appear among past winners. No minimum low-income percentage. Must be a school library (not a public library or after-school program) and tied to a specific project at a specific school. Past winners may reapply every year.
focus_areas: Books for school libraries serving disadvantaged children

grants.deadline_notes: Two cycles a year: applications for the Spring process are due February 1 and for the Fall process September 1. New applicants first submit an LOI in the grant portal (allow 10-14 business days for review) and, if approved, a full application. One application per organization per calendar year.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.typical_award: 2025 education grants: median $75,000; range $2,500 - $1,000,000 (111 grants)
grants.description: Fort Worth-based foundation whose charter requires all grants to go to recipients in Texas. Education and health grants can serve anywhere in Texas, though most recent education grants support Fort Worth-area programs, including a Catholic high school.
grants.geography: Texas (education and health statewide; human services and cultural grants limited to the Fort Worth area)
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) public charity or qualified public entity. No grants to individuals and no support for school trips, testimonial dinners, fundraisers or marketing events. Practical odds are highest for Fort Worth-area work.

grants.funder: Walmart Foundation (Walmart and Sam's Club facilities)
grants.deadline_notes: Walmart FY27 cycles: February 1 - April 15, May 1 - July 15, and August 1 - November 30 (the current cycle). Decisions are made before the next cycle opens.
grants.description: Cash grants from local Walmart stores, Sam's Clubs and distribution centers for organizations meeting a demonstrated need in the facility's service area. Faith-based organizations qualify only for projects that benefit the community at large.
grants.geography: National; apply to a Walmart or Sam's Club facility whose service area you serve
grants.eligibility_notes: Needs a Spark Good account verified by Deed. Nonprofit private K-12 schools qualify with an NCES number or 501(c)(3); churches and faith-based organizations only for projects benefiting the community at large (e.g. food pantries). Organizations that deny service or membership based on religion or other protected traits are excluded. Max 25 pending/approved applications; no reapplying to the same facility in the same fiscal year after being funded.
focus_areas: A specific, demonstrated need in the local community
Strengthening community (food access, disaster preparedness, connected communities)

grants.deadline_notes: The 2026 applications are closed (awards announced August 2026, check presentations September 2026); the next funding cycle opens in spring 2027.
grants.amount: Up to $5,000
grants.description: Funds school garden programs on school campuses: garden operations, program supplies, educator stipends and classroom cooking programs. Sister grants (Growing Healthy Kids; Wellness Across the Lifespan, also up to $5,000) fund community nutrition and wellness programs run by 501(c)(3) nonprofits.
grants.geography: States where Sprouts Farmers Market operates stores (includes Texas); ideal applicants are within 10 miles of a store
grants.eligibility_notes: The FAQ says applicants must be a public school or a 501(c)(3) nonprofit; private schools are not named, so a Catholic school would apply as a 501(c)(3) (e.g., under the USCCB group ruling) and should confirm with the foundation first. Program must run on the school campus. One Sprouts grant program per organization per cycle. Grants are funded by in-store Round Up donations that stay local.

grants.grant_name: Summerfield G. Roberts Foundation Grants (Texas History)
grants.deadline_notes: Proposals are due November 1 each year and reviewed at the co-trustees' February meeting; applications are mailed to the foundation's Dallas address listed on the Bank of America page.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: Dallas foundation whose Texas history program supports the study, teaching and dissemination of Texas history. A school could propose a defined Texas history teaching project (for example for the seventh-grade Texas history course).
grants.geography: Texas
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) organizations; two-page proposal letter with budget, key personnel, timeline, IRS letter, organizational history, board list and audit if any. Generally does not fund operating expenses; final report required.
focus_areas: Study, teaching, research and dissemination of Texas history
Graduate scholarships in business, finance and oil and gas

grants.grant_name: Teacher Development Grants and Academic Enrichment Grants
grants.deadline_notes: The online application is open January 15 - April 15 each year, or until 200 applications are received (it can close early, so apply soon after January 15, 2027). Applicants are notified July 15.
grants.amount: Up to $10,000 per year; one- or two-year grants (maximum $20,000 over two years)
grants.description: Grants to individual educators for classroom and extracurricular projects (Academic Enrichment) or for the professional growth of a teacher or small team (Teacher Development) that improve learning for students from low-income households.
grants.geography: National (foundation states no geographic restrictions)
grants.eligibility_notes: Grants go to individuals, never organizations. Teacher Development: licensed K-12 teachers employed in public OR private schools. Academic Enrichment: educators employed by schools or nonprofits with direct, regular contact with PreK-12 students. Both require working with students from low-income households. Note: Teacher Development asks for a licensed teacher; Texas private-school teachers without a state license should confirm with the foundation.
focus_areas: Students from low-income households (at-risk and under-funded)
Innovation in classrooms and education departments
Effectiveness of individual educators and small teacher teams

grants.deadline_notes: Two deadlines a year: January 15 (awards late April) and July 15 (awards late October), 5:00 p.m. Central, through the online grants portal. The Spring 2027 deadline is January 15, 2027.
grants.amount: Varies
grants.typical_award: Most FY2025-26 grants were $5,000 - $30,000
grants.description: Statewide foundation funding programs that enhance the rule of law and the justice system in Texas. A school could seek support for a civics or law-related education program such as a mock trial or courts unit.
grants.geography: Texas
grants.eligibility_notes: Projects must fit the foundation's mission. Applicant qualifications are shown only inside the grants portal preview; past grantees are 501(c)(3) charities and public bodies serving Texas. Confirm eligibility in the portal before applying.
focus_areas: Education about the third branch of government (civics and law-related education)

grants.grant_name: Texas Education Freedom Accounts (TEFA) - Private School Participation
grants.deadline_notes: Private schools can apply to participate at any time (rolling, through the TEFA school portal; school applications opened December 9, 2025). The 2026-27 family application window ran February 4 - March 31, 2026; 2027-28 family dates are not yet posted (interest list open). Private school students' funds arrive 25% July 1, 25% October 1 and 50% February 1.
grants.amount: $10,474 per participating private school student (2026-27); up to $30,000 for students with an IEP
grants.typical_award: $10,474 per private school student in 2026-27
grants.description: State education savings account program (Senate Bill 2, 2025) that lets awarded families pay an approved private school's tuition and fees from their account. An accredited Catholic school that registers as a participating school can enroll TEFA students and receive these payments.
grants.geography: Texas
grants.eligibility_notes: School must be accredited by an organization recognized by the Texas Private School Accreditation Commission (TEPSAC) or by TEA, have operated a campus for at least two years, give a nationally norm-referenced assessment (grades 3-12) and be in Texas. Pre-K/K providers have separate licensing and quality rules. Diocesan schools should confirm accreditation status with the diocesan schools office. Money flows through the family's account, not as a grant to the school.
focus_areas: Private school tuition and fees for awarded students

grants.deadline_notes: The FY2028 cycle is expected to open in early December 2026. In the FY2027 cycle, initial applications were due February 2, 2026, invited project proposals July 15, 2026, with awards in October 2026; expect a similar timeline.
grants.amount: $10,000 - $50,000 anticipated (1:1 cash match)
grants.typical_award: THC anticipated $10,000 - $50,000 awards for FY2027 ($330,000 available)
grants.description: Competitive state matching grants for preservation of historic architectural and archeological properties in Texas. Recently completed TPTF projects include a Catholic cathedral, so a parish with a designated historic church or school building can apply.
grants.geography: Texas
grants.eligibility_notes: Public or private owners of eligible historic properties may apply; the property must be listed in or determined eligible for a historic designation (National Register, Recorded Texas Historic Landmark, etc.). Dollar-for-dollar cash match, reimbursement basis; public access and benefit weigh in scoring. One application per cycle.
focus_areas: Restoration and preservation of historic buildings

grants.deadline_notes: Members direct their Choice Dollars any time during the year until December 31; Thrivent deposits grant funds electronically the month after a member directs them. An organization not yet in the catalog can be recommended by a Thrivent member.
grants.amount: Varies (member-directed)
grants.description: Christian fraternal benefit society's charitable grant program: members with Choice Dollars recommend where Thrivent sends grant funding, including churches and schools. Since 2010 it has distributed over $660 million, including $67 million to pre-K-12 schools and $386 million to congregations.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofits and churches enroll (often via member recommendation); Catholic schools appear in the Thrivent Choice catalog. Thrivent keeps final authority and does not fund organizations whose principal purpose is to influence law, policy or church doctrine. Funding depends on Thrivent members choosing the parish or school.
focus_areas: Christian camps, campus ministries and nonprofits

grants.deadline_notes: Applications accepted year-round through the online portal and scheduled for the quarterly board meetings (generally March, June, September and December) in the order received; responses come within two weeks of the meeting. Organizations that are not current grantees are invited to first email basic program information.
grants.amount: Varies (no more than 20% of the organization's operating budget)
grants.description: Austin-based family foundation funding programs that connect people to the tools and resources needed to build self-sufficient lives. For a school or parish, the realistic fit is a distinct youth-enrichment or children's-health program for low-income or at-risk children, not general school costs.
grants.geography: Greater Austin, Texas metropolitan area (also greater Chicago, which is closed to new applicants)
grants.eligibility_notes: 501(c)(3) required; organization must have existed at least five years. Will not fund public or private educational institutions for recurring operating, administrative or capital expenses (buildings, equipment) or scholarships that subsidize an existing scholarship base; will not fund school fundraisers, events or sports, or organizations that exclude participants based on race or religion. Religious organizations are not named as excluded.

grants.grant_name: Toshiba America Foundation K-12 Science/Math Grants
grants.deadline_notes: Grades 6-12, over $5,000: May 1 and November 1. Grades 6-12, $5,000 or less: March 1, June 1, September 1 and December 1 (the funder's home page calls this rolling). Grades K-5 (up to $1,000): October 1 each year, so the next K-5 deadline is October 1, 2027.
grants.amount: K-5: up to $1,000; 6-12: up to $5,000, or over $5,000 by larger-grant deadline
grants.description: Grants to K-12 teachers at public and private schools in the U.S. for teacher-designed, project-based STEM learning in their own classrooms.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: The foundation supports public and private schools throughout the U.S. 'Religious or political projects will not be supported', and organizations that discriminate on the basis of sex, race, age, disability or religion are not eligible. Not funded: general operations, capital, summer, club or after-school programs, salaries; requests solely for computers, laptops or tablets are generally not funded.
focus_areas: Grades K-5 and 6-12 science, technology, engineering and math

grants.funder: City of Austin (administered through Austin Community Foundation)
grants.deadline_notes: 2026 cycle: pre-submittal form and a required 30-minute pre-submittal meeting by October 1, 2026 (passed); applications open September 1 and due November 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.; awards in January 2027. Organizations that missed the October 1 meeting should plan for the next cycle (2026 pre-submittal meetings ran July - October).
grants.amount: Varies
grants.description: City-funded grants for stewardship projects that improve the long-term health of Austin's urban forest. Schools can use it for campus tree planting, tree care and tree education projects; neighborhoods with low Tree Equity Scores get priority.
grants.geography: City of Austin full-purpose jurisdiction only (project must be on civic property inside it)
grants.eligibility_notes: Eligible applicants include parent-teacher groups, academic and private institutions, nonprofits and community groups. Projects must be on civic property within the City of Austin's full-purpose jurisdiction; confirm in the pre-submittal meeting that a private school or parish campus qualifies.

grants.deadline_notes: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis; contact the USDA Rural Development state office (Texas) first to discuss the project.
grants.amount: Varies: low-interest direct loans and grants; grants on a graduated scale with higher percentages for small, low-income communities
grants.description: Loans and grants to buy, build or improve essential community facilities in rural areas and towns of up to 20,000 people. Eligible educational facilities include private schools; healthcare and public safety projects get priority.
grants.geography: Rural areas and towns of up to 20,000 population (Austin and its suburbs do not qualify)
grants.eligibility_notes: Applicants: public bodies, nonprofit corporations and federally recognized tribes. The project must serve an eligible rural area. Grant share depends on community population and income. Whether a religious school qualifies is decided by the state office.
focus_areas: Essential community facilities in rural areas
Educational facilities including private schools, libraries and museums

grants.grant_name: Vital Worship, Vital Preaching Grants for Worshiping Communities
grants.deadline_notes: Current round closes October 15, 2026 (applications opened July 15) for projects starting January 15, 2027; grants announced December 15, 2026. Twice-yearly program: proposal due dates in spring and fall 2027 will be announced.
grants.description: Ecumenical grants for year-long projects that renew public worship and connect it with intergenerational faith formation and discipleship. Parishes and religious schools are named as eligible, and recent grantees include Catholic projects.
grants.geography: United States and Canada
grants.eligibility_notes: Christian worshiping communities with tax-exempt status (congregations and parishes; seminaries, colleges and religious schools; hospitals and others). Team needs support of the pastor or key administrator. No grants to individuals, building renovations or construction; equipment capped at 10% and staff compensation at 20% of the grant.
focus_areas: Preaching, baptism and the Lord's Supper
Universal design and cultural engagement in worship

grants.deadline_notes: Recent cycles closed in April (April 18 in the 2025 guide; extended to April 30 in 2026), and applicants are notified by fall. The 2027 guidelines and dates were not posted as of October 15, 2026.
grants.amount: $2,000 to each of 50 finalists; three of them receive an additional $25,000, $10,000 or $5,000
grants.typical_award: $2,000 for each of 50 finalists (plus three top awards of $25,000 / $10,000 / $5,000)
grants.description: Awards to K-12 educators for innovative classroom projects that improve student learning, either existing projects or ones they want to launch. Award checks are payable jointly to the educator and the school and must be used for the project.
grants.geography: National
grants.eligibility_notes: Full-time educators, teachers, principals, paraprofessionals or classified staff employed by an accredited K-12 public OR private school in the US; awards are made without regard to creed or religion. Applications must be verified by a superintendent, principal or supervisor. Previous Unsung Heroes recipients cannot apply again. Voya client status is not required.

grants.grant_name: WeTeach_CS Preferred Provider Workshops (free summer CS, AI and cybersecurity PD for Texas teachers)
grants.funder: WeTeach_CS, Texas Advanced Computing Center, The University of Texas at Austin
grants.deadline_notes: 2027 workshops must run between June 7 and July 23, 2027; WeTeach_CS picks its providers by December 18, 2026 and then posts each workshop's page and application. In 2026, applications were reviewed on a rolling basis until spots filled (one AI workshop asked for applications by May 29, 2026).
grants.amount: Free PD of at least four days, plus stipends, travel help and/or classroom materials (2026 stipends ran from $80 a day up to $700, with travel reimbursement of up to $1,000 at one workshop)
grants.typical_award: $400 - $700 stipend (2026 workshops)
grants.description: WeTeach_CS pays curriculum providers to run free summer workshops, at least four days long, for Texas teachers in computational thinking, computer science, cybersecurity and AI. Participants get stipends, travel help and/or classroom kits. 2026 examples included ethical generative AI and data science with MIT App Inventor (grades 6-12) and a middle school machine-learning workshop with micro:bit kits. This is paid training with materials, not a school grant.
grants.geography: Texas (workshop sites vary; providers serving rural or underserved regions get priority)
grants.eligibility_notes: Texas educators. Each workshop sets its own grade band and priorities; for example, the 2026 App Inventor AI workshop was for Texas educators teaching grades 6-12 with priority to Title I schools, and some workshops were limited to one ESC region. No public-school-only rule was found.

grants.deadline_notes: The 2026 cycle opened June 1 and closed July 31, 2026; awards are announced the week of November 16, 2026. The 2027 dates have not been posted; expect a similar summer window.
grants.typical_award: 15 awards totaling $550,000 in 2026: $60,000 (winner, over two years), $30,000 (runner-up), $20,000 (semifinalist) per strategy area
grants.description: Unrestricted general operating grants advancing the economic mobility of women and children in Central Texas. The child care strategy (safe, quality, affordable child care for low-income families) is the closest fit for a parish or school early-childhood program.
grants.geography: Central Texas: Travis, Williamson, Hays, Bastrop, Burnet and Caldwell counties
grants.eligibility_notes: Same rules as the Hispanic Impact Fund: 501(c)(3) or government unit, budget of at least $50,000, two years of operation. Religious organizations may apply only for secular programming that does not discriminate against employees or clients based on religion. Note that one strategy area is unintended pregnancy prevention, which a Catholic applicant would not use.
focus_areas: Child care for families with low incomes

grants.funder: WeTeach_CS, Texas Advanced Computing Center, The University of Texas at Austin
grants.deadline_notes: The 2026 cycle closed April 17, 2026 (winners notified by May 4; projects run to May 31, 2027; final report due July 1, 2027). WeTeach_CS says to watch for 2027 mini-grants, $750 Change Maker Awards and Summit scholarships ahead of the 2027 WeTeach_CS Summit.
grants.amount: Up to $5,000
grants.description: Classroom mini-grants for Texas K-12 teachers with ideas to improve computer science teaching and learning, in school, after school or in summer camps. Money can buy CS teaching materials, justified technology, and LEGO Education Computer Science & AI kits and training. Winners must attend the June WeTeach_CS Summit, whose strands include AI and machine learning.
grants.geography: Texas
grants.eligibility_notes: Texas K-12 teachers in public, private or charter schools (private-school eligibility is stated on LEGO Education's page for the grant; the WeTeach_CS page does not mention school type). Past winners cannot win in back-to-back years; winners must attend the Summit, carry out the project as submitted and file a final report. Separately, 2026 Summit scholarships let Texas K-12 educators register for $50 instead of $800, with 2 hotel nights included.
focus_areas: Instructional resources and materials for K-12 Computer Science
After-school, summer camp or in-school CS projects

grants.deadline_notes: The 2027 Youth Garden Grant opens November 9, 2026 and closes December 11, 2026 (11:59 PM Pacific); grantees are notified late January 2027, awards arrive late February 2027, and a final report is due June 15, 2027.
grants.amount: $750 per program (30-50 awards), plus seeds; some winners receive sponsor packages (e.g., a container-garden package valued at $1,970)
grants.typical_award: $750 per grantee (fixed, 2027 round)
grants.description: Grants for new or improving school and youth garden programs that engage young people in gardening, distributed through sponsor-named awards such as a school garden award and garden champions awards.
grants.geography: National (U.S. and U.S. territories)
grants.eligibility_notes: Any U.S. organization planning a new garden program or improving an existing one that serves at least 15 youth ages 0-18 and supports or serves under-resourced communities; must have received less than $5,000 in garden-program grants in 2026; past KidsGardening grantees wait two years. Priority to programs reaching more than 50 youth with limited existing resources. (KidsGardening's separate Waterwise Garden Grant is limited to public and charter schools.)

foundations.application_cycle: Annual: Letters of Request January 1 - May 1; Board decides at its February meeting; notification by end of March
foundations.focus_areas: Direct evangelization, mass media, preparation of evangelists, capital expenditures (U.S. renovation), Catholic schools
foundations.notes: Catholic organizations listed in the Official Catholic Directory; one request per cycle; no more than 3 grants in 5 years; average award about $10,000.

foundations.application_cycle: Domestic Spring: January 1-15 (decision end of May); Domestic Fall: June 1-15 (decision end of November); International: May 1-15
foundations.focus_areas: Broad Catholic activities: education, social services, health, ministry and some construction
foundations.notes: U.S. applicants must be 501(c)(3) public charities listed in the Official Catholic Directory, with a bishop's letter. 2025 domestic grants: median $25,000.

foundations.application_cycle: Through the diocese: May 1 (dioceses on a January-December year) or November 1 (dioceses on a July-June fiscal year)
foundations.focus_areas: Mission (Extension) dioceses: churches and facilities, leaders, young Catholics, capacity building including Catholic schools, pastoral and social ministry
foundations.notes: Only the 87 pre-approved Extension dioceses may request funding; Texas Extension dioceses are Amarillo, Beaumont, Brownsville, El Paso, Laredo, Lubbock, San Angelo and Tyler (not Austin).

foundations.foundation_name: OSV Institute for Catholic Innovation (Our Sunday Visitor)
foundations.application_cycle: No open general grant cycle; CorWorks parish program application window October 9 - November 20, 2026
foundations.focus_areas: Catholic innovation, evangelization, parish response to local needs (Corporal Works of Mercy)
foundations.notes: Site has no grants guidelines page, only a grant portal login; the OSV Challenge ran 2019-2022; listed capacity grants date from 2018-2022. CorWorks offers parishes up to $25,000 in seed funding.

foundations.application_cycle: Initiative-based and by invitation; other requests start with a mailed preliminary letter of no more than two pages
foundations.focus_areas: Pastoral leadership, deepening Christian life, congregational vitality, strengthening religious institutions and networks, public understanding of religion
foundations.notes: Religion grantmaking is national but runs mostly through announced initiatives (e.g. Serving Neighbors Through Congregational Collaborations) and invited applicants; no unsolicited requests through the website contact form; no Catholic-school-specific initiative listed.

foundations.application_cycle: No application process; works with a focused set of partners
foundations.focus_areas: Alzheimer's prevention, global Church vitality, Thriving Local Community (Twin Cities Catholic schools), Catholic higher education
foundations.notes: Catholic-school support goes to selected Minneapolis/St. Paul partners; not a realistic source for a Texas school.

foundations.application_cycle: By invitation; does not accept unsolicited grant requests
foundations.focus_areas: Faith (building a vital Church, child protection, vital Catholic thought), education (children on the margins), criminal justice, purposeful business
foundations.notes: U.S. office covers Canada, Haiti and the United States; Porticus states it 'cannot accept unsolicited requests for grants'.

foundations.foundation_name: FADICA (Foundations and Donors Interested in Catholic Activities)
foundations.application_cycle: N/A - peer network, not a grantmaker
foundations.focus_areas: Network of Catholic philanthropies; initiatives include Catholic education, Catholic social tradition, Laudato Si' and next-generation philanthropy
foundations.notes: Does not take grant applications. Its Catholic Funding Guide (catholicfundingguide.com, paid subscription) lists more than 1,800 Catholic funders and is the practical way to use FADICA for prospecting. City comes from a third-party nonprofit listing; the FADICA site gives no street address.
